citations.title: Simon Trott

sentences.text: Simon Trott became Chief Executive of Rio Tinto on 25 August 2025, succeeding Jakob Stausholm.

sentences.quote: He has been on the Executive Committee since 2018, most recently as Chief Executive, Iron Ore, which he helped reshape through financial discipline and improvements in operational and safety performance.
sentences.text: He had served on the Executive Committee since 2018, most recently as Chief Executive, Iron Ore, which he helped reshape through financial discipline and improvements in operational and safety performance, and before that as Rio Tinto's first Chief Commercial Officer, following managing director roles across multiple Rio Tinto commodities and geographies.

He has worked across Rio Tinto's global operations, including three years as chief commercial officer in Singapore, and managed its salt, uranium, borates and diamonds units in Australia, Namibia, the United States, Canada and Serbia.
An Australian national, he led the iron ore division from 2021 and relocated to London for the chief executive role.

citations.title: Rio Tinto: Solid results underpinned by +8% CuEq production and sharper cost discipline

sentences.text: Simon Trott became chief executive in August 2025 after running the iron ore division, which the board credited with improved operational performance, reset stakeholder partnerships and new mine developments.

At the 2025 Capital Markets Day he set out a "stronger, sharper and simpler" plan to release $5-10 billion through divestments and productivity, with an operating model built around aluminium, lithium, copper and iron ore.

sentences.quote: Ordinary dividend of $6.5 billion, a 60% payout, ten-year track record at top end of range.
sentences.text: FY2025 brought underlying earnings of $10.9 billion, completion of the Oyu Tolgoi underground project, first Simandou shipment and Western Range delivered on time and on budget, alongside a $6.5 billion dividend at a 60% payout, a ten-year record at the top of the range; net debt rose to $14.4 billion and underlying ROCE eased to 16% from 18%.
